messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — we're planning a staggered maintenance window tonight for the runtime: pinning a model variant (gpt-redwood-1.9.2-quant) and a kernel upgrade. Change window: 23:00-01:30 UTC. This is a rolling, region-by-region update to avoid global capacity loss.

arjun: +1. Are we forcing pin for Dedicated customers or only Hosted fallbacks?

maya: For Dedicated we'll apply optional pinning (customer can opt-out) — Hosted will get an automated fallback policy: if a new variant fails, requests will go to 1.9.1. No data-plane schema changes.

sam (support): Drafting customer comms now. Can you confirm what to put on statuspage and whether to include a recommended client retry header?

maya: Yes include a short note about "temporary elevated latency in affected regions" and the retry header suggestion: Retry-After: 5s for 429s during the window. Also mention dedicated customers can request a maintenance hold.

lia: Any rollback criteria we should call out? error-rate > 2% for 5m or p95 latency spike > 2x baseline?
arjun: Let's use both. If error-rate > 1.5% sustained for 10m during canary we'll pause and investigate. For global rollout, threshold is 1%. Keep ops oncall ready.

maya: Deploy bot scheduled a canary at 23:05 UTC for eu-west-1, then us-west-2 at 23:30, ap-south-1 at 00:15. Cascade only after canaries meet SLOs.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy started — canary eu-west-1 — runtime v1.9.2-pin (id: db-1750001111-1). Expected duration ~15m.

opsbot: canary-healthcheck: p50=45ms p95=120ms errors=0.2% (baseline p95=110ms errors=0.15%) — OK to continue? :white_check_mark:

arjun: Looks fine. Proceed to us-west-2.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy started — canary us-west-2 — runtime v1.9.2-pin (id: db-1750001111-2).

opsbot: canary-healthcheck: p50=50ms p95=240ms errors=1.8% — hitting threshold. Pausing automated rollout. :warning:

maya: Pausing. Rolling back us-west-2 canary to 1.9.1 and opening an incident channel for investigation. Sam, please prepare a short statuspage update saying "canary paused due to increased errors in one region — investigation underway; no widespread impact detected."

sam (support): On it — draft below. Please review.

sam (support): ```Status: Investigating
Component: Runtime inference (Regional)
Impact: Some requests in us-west-2 experiencing elevated errors and latency during a canary deploy.
What's happening: We rolled a canary for runtime v1.9.2-pin; our monitoring detected an error-rate spike in us-west-2, so the automated rollout was paused and the canary rolled back.
What we're doing: Engineering is investigating the regression. Affected region remains on the previous stable runtime. No action required by customers at this time.
ETA: We'll provide updates within 30 minutes or sooner.```

maya: LGTM. Add the opt-out/dedicated note: "Dedicated customers can request a maintenance hold — contact support@redwood.ai"

sam (support): Added and published to statuspage.

lia: Postmortem checklist: capture kernel traces, compare quantization path timings, diff request logs between 1.9.1 and 1.9.2 for failing traces. Also dump KV cache hit rates for canary pods.
arjun: Assigning to @lia + @maya for triage; escalate to ML infra if kernel-level culprit.

maya: Noting action items in the incident doc. Will follow up with a short release note update after root cause.

sam (support): Customer outbound email draft (short): "We performed a canary deploy for a runtime update and paused the rollout after elevated errors were observed in a single region. We've reverted that region to the previous runtime and are investigating. There is no action required. We'll send a follow-up with root cause and mitigation." Any edits?
arjun: fine. Add line: "If you rely on pinned versions, no changes were made to existing pinned Dedicated allocations."
sam (support): Added and queued to send to customers subscribed to maintenance updates.

maya: Thanks all. We'll reconvene in 20 for status update. :clock1:
